#3703. One Company Is Giving All Of Its 7,000 Employees The Day Off To Play GTA 6

Logitech, rather than processing the no-doubt massive load of time-off requests that would all mysteriously happen to fall on the same day, is just declaring November 19th its Logi Game Day and letting everybody take it off. Why November 19th? Guess.

It’s a day off, don’t let Logitech tell you what to do with it. No matter what its employees decide to do with their time, the company is smartly getting ahead of economists’ prognostications about just how much GTA VI will cost the economy in folks calling out of work to play by just dialing its productivity for the day down to zero.

What’s especially funny is that the press release for the event frontloads a bunch of statistics that talk about how gaming is good for professional performance. “In the companyâs recent Logitech Ctrl Tomorrow study, 81% of gamers believe that gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety, and correlates with stronger day-to-day work performance.”

Yes, these things are probably true. But let’s not pretend that saying “As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other” is anything but the corporate version of handing your gym teacher a forged note from your mom saying it’s okay to skip class, except your gym teacher in this case is Logitech shareholders and your mom is GTA VI.

Tony DiNozzo's return and subsequent promotion to Director of NCIS is the big story of Season 24. It was a surprising twist, and one that longtime fan and star Katrina Law told CinemaBlend she was amped for. It turns out she had a lot of questions about how Jessica Knight and Tony would interact, and she loved what the team came up with.

As NCIS continues its run on the 2026 TV schedule, I spoke to Law about the season thus far, as well as what we've seen. I talked about Michael Weatherly's big role in the new season, and she confirmed she was absolutely psyched to see the former vet of the show back in action:

I was geeked out. I've been an OG fan of the show, and Weatherly and actually Tiva has been my favorite part of the show, and I kept pitching all of these ideas of like, oh, what could Weatherly and Knight's relationship be?How do we meet? What's going to happen? And not once did I ever think I would be the informant for Ziva about his caloric intake. I love it. I think it's hysterical.

While she might've preferred to see her buddy McGee get the job as NCIS director, Jessica Knight has found good footing with Tony thus far. Granted, she's basically playing spy for his wife Ziva, but that kind of leverage can go a long way toward keeping her in his good graces.

I also had to bring up that Knight mentioning on camera that she's in contact with Ziva sets the stage for Cote de Pablo's eventual return to NCIS as well. Katrina Law confirmed she's optimistic we'll see Ziva before too long, and there's going to be a lot of fun stuff happening with her and Knight:

I fully expect Ziva to come onto our show and Knight and Ziva team up and just make Weatherly extremely uncomfortable, but then go off and like have a massive fight scene together to take down some bad guy.

She's been thinking about this team-up for a while, for the record, and I'm so excited for the day it finally happens. For now, she'll continue to solve crimes with her team and keep Tony on his toes with her occasional trolling of his eating habits.

Tony needs that so far, as he continues to look for ways to settle into his new role at the top of the NCIS team. He's tried to jump in and participate in the investigations, much to the chagrin of some of the agents. We'll see if he gets any better at taking a step back, letting them do their jobs, and watching from the sidelines and offering any support he can.

Being the director is not an easy job, and one that's filled with hazards. In fact, the past few NCIS directors have died, which may have fans sweating and wondering just how long Tony will sit in the role. Will he step away before he ends up in a body bag, or will he break the trend and end up staying at the top until retirement hits?

NCIS continues on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. Tune in for more of the team as they track down the bad guys and get to know each other better. I'm excited for more interactions between Jessica and Tony, and that eventual team-up with Ziva that's on the way.

#3701. Paradox boss Frederik Wester stepping down after several tumultuous years for the Cities Skylines and Stellaris publisher

Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja taking over role.

Paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the company. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level."

Wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a new studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus."

Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

#3699. The Witcher 3 Devs Explain Using AI To Help With Geralt’s Polish Voice In Songs Of The Past: ‘This Is One Of Those Ways Where You Can Use AI Ethically’

CD Projekt RedGeraltSongs of the PastThe Witcher 3

Voice actor Jacek Rozenek plays Geralt of Rivia in the Polish version of The Witcher 3, but in 2019 he suffered a stroke that made it hard to speak and changed his voice. CD Projekt Red faced a choice for the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion: swap actors, or turn to AI to help match Rozenek’s new performance with the one he did for the 2015 release. The studio chose the latter.

âI can tell you, as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a big concern,â localization producer MikoÅaj Szwed told Game File in a new interview about the process. He added, “I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good.”

Game File reports that CDPR turned to Ukrainian AI voice cloning firm Respeecher for help, the same company it worked with when one of the voice actors for Cyberpunk 2077 died between the release of the original game release and that of the Phantom Liberty expansion. It trains an algorithm on someone’s existing voice work in order to match new performances to the tone and style of the originals. The actors, or their estates, have to consent.

“The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago,” Rozenek told Game File. “I have great trustâ¦for the creators of this game.” He continued, “When it comes to the dynamics of the voice, when it comes to the acting aspects, I feel very good, really very good,â he said. âI can play this role. Of course, itâs very good that this voice will be matched.”

The actor recorded over 10,000 lines for the original game, work that Respeecher used in creating its algorithm for his voice. âGetting there took dozens of hours, training models, going through the details with the CDPR team, and dealing with AI artifacts that never fully disappear,â Dmytro Vasylets, a synthetic speech artist for the company, told Game File. âThe hardest part was Jacekâs emotional range: the half-tones, shouts, groans, anger, fear and laughter. Capturing all of that at the highest audio quality was the real challenge. Iâd like to think we pulled it off.â

CDPR said it wasn’t planning to use the algorithm to alter Rozenek’s voice in the future, suggesting that his now lower, gruffier voice would be fine for the appearance of an older, gruffier Geralt in a game like The Witcher 4. The voice actor, meanwhile, confirmed he has not listened to his AI doppelganger and it doesn’t sound like he’s planning to anytime soon.

#3698. After two weeks of multiplayer downtime, Dark Souls 2 & 3's mysterious server "issue" has been fixed, so it no longer feels so lonely online

Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server issue". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

FromSoftware never specified the exact issue impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding."

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

This isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

For over 20 years now, the 2003 Mike Myers version of The Cat In The Hat has been the only version of the classic Dr. Seuss book to watch. However, this past weekend, it got the animation treatment, and it’s a blast of an adaptation. I even have an idea for a spinoff, and I ran it by some of the cast. SPOILERS ahead!

Look, I like The Cat, especially because he’s voiced by Bill Hader years after he played the character on SNL. But to me, the real highlight of the film are The Things. In my opinion, they are like much more likeable Minions, and the movie even explores what can happen to one when they get villainous. As we learn at the end of The Cat In The Hat, the reason why Thing 2 was missing is that he became The Something due to overusing the Go-Backer device. Oh, and of course there’s that meta line where The Cat tells The Things to wait for their own movie.

The Things are pretty mysterious characters, but I thought The Cat in the Hat did an excellent job of making them so fun and intriguing. I think it would be so much fun to see them on their own adventure after this movie earned a thumbs-up with audiences through an “A” CinemaScore. Though it’ll have to earn more money at the box office after Godzilla Minus Zero won the weekend.

When CinemaBlend spoke to the cast of The Cat In The Hat, I brought up the topic of a Things spinoff. Here’s what Abbott Elementary’s Quinta Brunson, a.k.a. Sherrie from HR in the movie, had to say:

I wanna learn everything about them. This movie opening the crate, so to speak, on The Thing world, made me wanna know way more. I still have a lot of questions. Like, are they related? Are they from a planet? Is there offspring? Do they fall in love? Do they get married? I have a lot of questions. Why are they numbered? Do they have names beyond the numbers?

I love all these questions she has about The Things, because I had many of them myself. The Things have always been a memorable part of The Cat In The Hat book, but it would be so fun for a spinoff to explore who they are without The Cat. Here’s what Mr. Hoogeboom voice actor Giancarlo Esposito added:

I'm fascinated by The Things. I think they're on some advanced level of intellectual and emotional feeling. I just think that they're simpler, and somehow they communicate in a way that's clearer than any words could ever get.

I feel like a lot of kids are going to start learning Thinglish as is, and I wanted my own Thing plushy the moment I finished the movie. I even brought it up to the writer/directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni. Here’s what Carloni had to say about my idea:

If we're so lucky that the audience wants more of the characters we created, that would be very flattering. Give them what they want.

We’ll have to wait and see if this becomes a reality! For now, you can watch The Cat In The Hat only in theaters.

#3696. The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"

"I have great trust ... for the creators of this game."

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game."

Game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce new voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

"For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference."

The third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game launched. It adds an entirely new region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

In preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

#3695. Marvel 1943 ‘Has Not Been Canceled,’ Says Skydance Leadership, Despite Development Struggles

Today, a rumor began to spread that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was about to be canceled. But according to a source on the project, developers are being reassured that it is not, in fact, canceled, despite ongoing struggles.

The news of a cancelation announcement was first spread by fan account Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown, and was quickly picked up in fan circles. However, before it could be confirmed or elaborated upon, executive producer Lu Gigliotti posted a message in the Skydance Slack (viewed by Kotaku) stating that he had spoken “directly” with the “executive leadership team (Dan [Prigg], Shawn [Kittelson], Andrea [Benavides], etc.) [all Skydance employees]” and that the game was not canceled. “They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly. There is no truth to these claims.” Developers were told not to let the rumor distract them, and that the studio was “monitoring the situation” and would address it “through the appropriate channels.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was begun as Amy Hennig’s project within the newly established Skydance New Media in 2019. It was teased in 2022 and fully revealed in 2024, with plans to release in holiday of 2025. The game would have been an action-adventure starring Captain America, Black Panther, Gabriel Jones, and Nanali as they take down the budding terrorist organization Hydra.

According to the Slack post, the game is approaching an “Alpha” milestone later this month, though Kotaku understands it has run into significant, repeated trouble throughout its development. Marvel 1943 was first delayed to “beyond early 2026” and then further delayed into 2027 and beyond. The original pitch for Marvel 1943 was as a Netflix game, but it transitioned to a console and PC game during development. As a result, its current rendition is light on gameplay, primarily using only one button and lacking significant interaction. It is also well over budget, and has been significantly cut back from its original vision both in terms of length and content. Kotaku’s source says the project is now “close to done.”

Just two days ago, at least 30 people at Paramount Games were laid off in the wake of the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros., Those impacted included many from Skydance, though the exact number remains unclear, and it does not appear to have had significant impact on the Marvel 1943 team.

Kotaku has reached out to both Skydance and Marvel for comment.

Helldivers 2, in the running for the most review-bombed game in history, got another Steam beating a few weeks back when Arrowhead announced a change in anti-cheat services that would break or disallow existing mods.

The goal with the switch from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat, as the studio explained at the time, was to combat mods that "create unfair advantages or negatively impact others," but it also acknowledged that mods it has no problems with, like cosmetic add-ons, would also be affected. The news went over like a lead balloon, prompting over 10,000 fresh negative Steam reviews and a "mostly negative" recent rating.

Skimming the last few weeks of ratings, negative reviewers are either miffed about their broken mods, new and old bugs, or the perception that Arrowhead is attacking modders instead of fixing bugs. There was no reality where a community notorious for intensely boycotting everything it finds annoying was going to embrace stricter modding oversight, but Arrowhead did address the outcry in its latest Helldivers 2 developer blog.

"We added Easy Anti-Cheat for one reason: to reduce the number of cheaters joining your missions and ruining the experience. On that front, we think we’re taking steps in the right direction," the blog read. "However, we do see that this change means that some PC players lost the use of fan-made game mods. While all mods are not officially supported, we have been reviewing how the code changes disabled cosmetic non-gameplay mods. This has resulted in adjustments that should allow some cosmetic mods to be functional with our next hotfix."

Mod restriction is a prickly topic for Helldivers 2, which is both a perfectly valid candidate for mods as a purely PvE game, but also a live service with real-money currency and DLC. A common form of cheating in Helldivers 2 is to use mods to farm (or straight up spawn) premium Super Credits that are supposed to be rare. Another is to alter weapon or enemy behavior in ways that are unfair to vanilla teammates trying to play normally, or in some cases cause client crashes.

I'm guessing Arrowhead is slightly more concerned about the folks farming free currency at rapid speeds than the ones with infinite ammo cheats, but it won't be budging on outlawing gameplay-altering mods that, "from a technical perspective, are indistinguishable from an attempt to cheat."

But that's not the only thing the Reddit crowd is pissed about: The studio also acknowledged that promised improvements to hellpod steering and stratagem bouncing have taken longer than planned because they "require substantial adjustments to both mechanics while taking into account all edge cases," copped to missing patch dates on its current roadmap, and apologized for overselling the arrival of bug caves on more map types as a "new biome" on the same roadmap.

"Your input matters and we’re sorry this roadmap wasn’t as accurate as it should have been, Helldivers. While we aren’t announcing a date for it in this article, our next roadmap will demonstrate the impact of your feedback."

Looking ahead, Arrowhead shared some improvements coming in early December:

Good stuff, except I have read that first bullet point three times now and still can't decide what it means. I think it means that mobility packs now pair nicely with objectives that require carrying large objects, like SEAF artillery missiles, but I'm just not sure. I suppose they did say they're working on clarity.

I would like to begin this story about Julie Chen Moonves commenting on the future of Big Brother by noting the longtime host of the CBS reality series is not planning an exit anytime soon. There will, well likely, be no goodbye episode for her in the near future, but given the show’s popularity, I’d be willing to bet she’ll retire before Big Brother is off the air. She’s seen the conversations surrounding her exit, and she’s honestly in agreement.

So, first let’s talk about the fan speculation. As recently as three months ago, some fans were speculating they think Julie Chen Moonves will leave Big Brother after Season 30. Season 28 just wrapped with Rick Devens as the winner, and the show airs in the summer, which would give her a couple more seasons on the TV schedule before bowing out. Of course, this is complete speculation, and the reality host has not said anything either way.

In other threads, fans have mentioned thinking that Big Brother and Amazing Race contestant, and Big Brother: Unlocked star could be the ideal choice. Honestly, it’s been a bit divisive, with some fans noting:

Even though the issue is apparently divisive, I know in general Big Brother fans can be haters and in many ways Hale would be an obvious and solid choice. The people worried about her being too polished in particular I think are reading into it hard. Chen Moonves herself is polished, professional and deeply unemotional as the host. I honestly think Hale would be a nice segue if the OG host were to leave. She may not be for everyone, but Chen Moonves isn't for everyone either.

I guess what I'm saying is it's impossible to make everyone happy, and Julie Chen Moonves is not a hater when it comes to Taylor Hale. In an interview with Variety, the interviewer casually mentioned the possibility of Taylor Hale taking over, and this is what Chen Moonves had to say.

I’ve wondered that too because, to me, she would be perfect.

She did tell the outlet Big Brother has had so many notable names that would be as solid as Hale, also name-dropping BB and Traitors' Derrick Levasseur, Jeff Schroeder and Jordan Lloyd. Her one takeaway though?

But then I don’t know how the network would feel about, ‘Is it too close to home that they’ve walked in their shoes? Does that put them too much in a position of judgment?' Part of me feels like maybe you want to keep the air pristine and have someone who comes from a news background. I got hired because I know how to do live interviews.

Interestingly, she actually talked about how she got the gig on Big Brother recently, telling fellow reality host Phil Keoghan CBS wanted someone with a news background to do the work on the show. At the time, it was heavily a social experiment as much as a reality show, and her background fed into that.

It would change things if Julie Chen Moonves were to leave, but I do think another contestant would be close enough to the franchise to step into her shoes flawlessly, and Taylor and Derek in particular do have the background to potentially do so.

Of course, this is if and when she ever steps down. She previously told EW she was "playing a game of chicken" with CBS' Jeff Probst and Phil Keoghan and would stick it out as long as they would. (Note: Jeff and Phil are also both older than the 56-year-old star is at 65 and 59 respectively.) We'll have to wait and see what happens, but I'm just saying, don't expect an announcement tomorrow.

Jacek Rozenek was the voice of Geralt in all previous Polish-language Witcher releases, and CD Projekt wanted to work with him again—but his voice is no longer a match.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Game File reports that CD Projekt worked with AI company Respeecher to modify the voice of Geralt's Polish voice actor in the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.

The actor, Jacek Rozenek, voiced Geralt in the Polish editions of all the Witcher games, including The Witcher 3 and its two expansions, and the Game File report says his performances are highly regarded. But in 2019, he had a stroke that left him temporarily unable to speak; by 2021 he had rehabilitated enough to be able to provide some new lines for The Witcher 3's next-gen update, but the process left him "exhausted."

Still, he continued to train and was eventually able to return to work, and when CD Projekt decided to make a new Witcher 3 expansion it wanted him back for the role. But the stroke, and the passage of time, had left Rozenek's voice noticeably changed. Given that Songs of the Past will occur in the midst of The Witcher 3, that shift in tone—"lower [and] gruffer," according to Game File's Stephen Totilo—presented a problem.

So with Rozenek's permission, CD Projekt approached AI voice company Respeecher to rework his voice for the game. Rozenek is still providing the voice of Geralt in the Polish version of the expansion, but Respeecher is adjusting it to make him sound like he did a decade ago.

"The brief was simple: make Jacek’s voice sound alive, rich and young, like in the original game," synthetic speech artist Dmytro Vasylets said.

"Getting there took dozens of hours, training models, going through the details with the CDPR team, and dealing with AI artifacts that never fully disappear. The hardest part was Jacek’s emotional range: the half-tones, shouts, groans, anger, fear and laughter. Capturing all of that at the highest audio quality was the real challenge. I’d like to think we pulled it off."

Rozenek said he feels "very good" about returning to the role of Geralt because he's so familiar with the character; the issue was merely that his voice was different. Because of that, he's all in favor of the AI treatment: "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," he said. "I have great trust…for the creators of this game."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't CD Projekt's first time working with Respeecher: It previously used the company to reproduce the voice of Miłogost Reczek, who portrayed Viktor Vektor and Vesemir in the Polish releases of Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3. Reczek died in 2021; in that case, CD Projekt had the family's blessing to use an AI recreation of the actor's voice.

The use of generative AI in voice acting is an incredibly thorny issue, one that voice actors have gone to great lengths to maintain some control over. CD Projekt itself has been ambivalent about AI; localization producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File that "as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a big concern," although he added that "this was a special case" caused by Rozenek's health problems. The studio is not planning to do anything similar with the voice of Doug Cockle, who portrays Geralt in the English releases of The Witcher games, Szwed said; Rozenek's voice would also not be altered in any hypothetical future Witcher games set later in the timeline, because the vocal change would be explainable: "It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other."

Interestingly, the news of Rozenek's AI-powered vocal overhaul comes just one day after veteran voice actor Stephen Russell appeared in a Nightdive podcast and discussed returning to the role of Garrett in the upcoming Thief: The Dark Project remaster. It's been more than 20 years since Russell last portrayed the character, in 2004's Thief: Deadly Shadows, which meant he had to be more conscious of his pitch and delivery while working on content for the new Tarnished Mirror expansion.

But while "the equipment changes," as Russell said, Rozenek's stroke created a more substantial change: Totilo said his untouched voice in the expansion "sounds deep and gravelly, noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game," while the AI-edited voice is much closer to Rozenek's voice as it was a decade ago.

Actress Jessica Chastain has had a busy year, with the release of a number of exciting projects. Her new horror movie titled Other Mommy arrived in theaters back in October, and she's got a mystery thriller called Heartland coming out for those with a Netflix subscription. It turns out she got so into character on set that her face actually changed. No, she didn't use makeup to make that happen.

Chastain's Other Mommy face went viral when the movie came out, thanks to the unsettling smile slapped on her face during the movie's runtime. As you can see in the video above, I asked the Oscar-winning actress to compare the physical transformation she had for that movie and Heartland, and she told me:

I noticed something which, this is the first time I saw it in a character. I had so much kind of like anger playing Misty and like, I felt like very sensitive. Even though she's angry, I just felt like Misty should be so sensitive and so wounded that she can get hurt really easily so she reacts almost like an abused animal would react.

She's not wrong. Having seen the movie early, Misty does feel like an abused animal at times. There's a palpable sense of anger and hurt throughout most of her scenes, sometimes coming to a boil with Chastain vandalizing the property of her enemies. I loved watching her pop off throughout the movie's 112-minute runtime, mostly because I wish I could be so unapologetic IRL.

Later in our same conversation, the Mama actress went on to share how her character's anger physically manifested in her face when shooting Heartland. As she told me:

And I have like my chin in this movie has a dimple like on the side from tension that I'm holding that I've never seen before in a character that I've played. Um, and it was the first time I was like, 'Oh wow, that's so interesting that whatever I was feeling as this character changed my face a little bit. I mean, I guess it goes to show how powerful emotions are that they can physically change what you look like.

How trippy is that? Even Jessica Chastain was surprised by how playing Misty physically affected her. She's likely seen her own face on screen countless times over the years, so it was noticeably when a new dimple on her chin suddenly appeared. That shows just how deep into character she was while shooting Heartland. This commitment is a big reason why she's had such a celebrated career.

Fans will get to see her transformation into fictional country singer Misty Jones when Heartland arrives on Netflix November 13th as part of the 2026 movie release list. In addition to having drama and action, Chastain also belts out some country tunes in the new thriller.

#3689. Hey, Nintendo, What’s Going On With Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s Most Insufferable Couple?

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

I’ve been gushing for a few days now about some of the smaller details added to Hyrule in the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, like this new dialogue in Castle Town and new clarity on the fate of the Zora. But last night I ran into another deeply silly addition that I just have to tell you about. It’s controversy! Scandal! Confusion?

What the heck is going on with Honey and Darling?

If you don’t know who Honey and Darling are, you’ve definitely seen them before. They’re the perpetually dancing couple who appear in the center square of Hyrule Castle Town, and then move to the hilltop behind the windmill in Kakariko Village in the adult era. In the original Ocarina of Time, they are unnamed, but Majora’s Mask canonized their alternate selves as Honey and Darling. Ocarina of Time has them using those same nicknames for one another, so in the interest of clarity, I’m going to refer to them here, too, as Honey (the woman) and Darling (the man).

Honey and Darling are iconic and insufferable. In the original game, they sit there and gush over how in love they are with one another, with Honey comparing Darling to the handsome King of Hyrule and Darling saying Honey is more beautiful than Princess Zelda. They continue spinning on and on into the night, day after day. In Kakariko, they’reÂ still spinning, offering Link no useful information when he speaks to them but instead calling him “annoying” and accusing him of “violating” their “personal space.” If you approach them wearing one of the game’s many masks, they still express nothing more interesting than irritation with you for daring to exist. Rude! I just wanted to chat!

From all that, you can interpret little more than that Honey and Darling are obsessively in love with one another, get some sort of kick out of publicly displaying that love, and are still together in spite of their mutual insufferability (or perhaps because of it) seven years later. Fine, unremarkable.

In the remake, though! This pair is back, seemingly the same as ever, albeit with some more dialogue that has each of them gushing over their respective partner. Nothing to see here, right? Wrong.Â Put on that Mask of Truth!

The Mask of Truth is an item received from the Happy Mask Salesman sidequests that, when donned, allows you to read the minds of most characters. Unlike in the original, here you can wear masks as both child and adult Link, which gives you double the opportunities to see what’s really going on in people’s heads. The Mask of Truth dialogue adds a lot of humor and context to many of the game’s interactions, but in the case of Honey and Darling, it has utterly baffled me. Get a load of this:

That’s Darling speaking! What! What the hell, man?! You don’t even know this woman’s name and you’ve been spinning around this square declaring your love for her for how long? How many other women are you seeing? Sheesh! When paired with Honey’s dialogue posted above (“If he ever hurts me, I’ll never forgive him…”), this suggests something a little ominous for the future of their relationship, right?

So let’s check in on them in Kakariko Village, seven years in the future. Still dancing, still obsessing over one another. Except…

Excuse me?! That’s Honey speaking this time! The younger twin ofÂ whom?! As far as I’m aware, Honey having a twin has never once come up. Unless…okay, I’m putting it together here. Darling is dating a pair of twin sisters. He knows they’re twins, but can’t keep their names straight. Honey (and Honey 2, I guess) are also aware of this arrangement and don’t care, but the younger of the two seems a bit dismayed that Darling can’t tell them apart.

I’ve been trying to do reporter work all day, looking around both towns for a double of Honey hiding somewhere, but I’ve come up empty. I’ve tried Mask of Truthing everyone in the vicinity to see if anyone knows anything about what’s happening here and will comment on it, but it’s no good. I am left with only theories as to what sort of bizarre relationship is going on between these two, maybe three, people. You might say, “Reb, this is none of your business!” To that I say, Honey and Honey and Darling made it my business when they started dramatically parading their romance in the town square. For all of their sakes, however many of them there are, I hope every member of this relationship is clued in as to the presence of every other person within it. Otherwise, I’m predicting some serious scandal come Majora’s Mask time.

#3688. These Surprisingly Powerful Soundcore Earbuds Are Under $35 Right Now

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

The Soundcore P31i earbuds are down to $32.99 (originally $59.99), which is as low as they’ve been, according to price trackers. At this price, most earbuds stick to the basics, so it’s unusual to see features like active noise cancellation and LDAC included here. That doesn’t mean they compete with premium pairs, but they do give you more to work with than you’d expect for under $35.

These earbuds are light, they fit well, and they don’t get uncomfortable after an hour or two, which isn’t always the case with cheaper earbuds. Battery life, too, holds up through a full day of use, with a little over seven hours on a single charge and extra top-ups from the case. The sound quality is better than expected for the price, though it leans toward bass-heavy tuning out of the box (you can tweak it in the app, but the app itself is not the most intuitive and takes some getting used to, notes this ZDNET review), and if you’re using a compatible device, LDAC support gives you the option for better audio quality.

There are also a few extras tucked in, like HearID for tuning the sound to your ears and an AI translation feature, though features like that feel more like a bonus than something you will use every day. As for its noise cancellation, it works, but expectations need to stay in check—it reduces steady background noise like engines and traffic, but it won’t match the isolation you get from more expensive earbuds. That lines up with its overall build, as well, which feels a bit basic compared to more expensive options.

While the Nvidia board reportedly mulls over the idea of ousting CEO Jensen Huang, after his admission of an affair and suspicions of another have come to light, some powerful figures in the tech industry have taken to X to give comment.

Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has put forward perhaps the strongest advocacy for keeping the Nvidia chief in place, beginning with the phrase "Save Jensen."

Save Jensen. This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from NVIDIA’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America. The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.November 12, 2026

"This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America," says Sweeney. "The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers"

Given Sweeney's well-documented advocacy of the wonders of AI, it's perhaps no surprise that he's leaping to the defence of one of its chief architects. Elon Musk, meanwhile, has responded to an X user asking him to hire Huang, presumably if everything goes south with the Nvidia board.

"That would be an honor," said Musk, before the thread inevitably descends into AI-generated images of what a Huang/Musk teamup might look like.

@zerohedge That would be an honorNovember 12, 2026

Would Huang really rehash the old "let that sink in" joke for giggles? I doubt it, but we're living in strange and uncertain times. Allegations of a second affair with an Nvidia executive have cast further doubt on Huang's future at the company, with many already speculating on his potential replacement.

An Nvidia without Jensen Huang seems like a truly bizarre situation to imagine. There's no word yet as to a decision from the Nvidia board of directors, who are reported to have met on Wednesday to decide Huang's fate. The company's share price has slid dramatically since the first allegations, and the company's stock was down 6.3% in premarket trading this morning.

Still, Huang's leadership at Nvidia has been characterised by partnerships with other tech leaders, and it seems some would be reluctant to see him go. Or, in the case of Musk, eager to bring him into the fold within their own organisations. A mere week or two ago, Huang seemed like an unstoppable force within the tech space—time will tell whether that resilience holds.

Long-running TV shows are usually wildly popular but that doesn't mean that they aren't without faults. Even shows that actually ended well have certain characters that fans simply cannot stand. Fans recently spoke about this over on Reddit, and Xander from Buffy the Vampire Slayer (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) isn't the only one being name dropped.

A popular Reddit thread started this week, where TV fans ranted about one character from their favorite shows that lowkey ruin it. One popular response was about Xander from Buffy, with the comment reading:

I find Xander Harris from Buffy the vampire slayer insufferable. The misogynistic writing around Xander's character hasn't aged well at all and on top of him being a self insert by a sexist writer definitely doesn't help.

Xander was played by late actor Nicholas Brendan throughout all seven seasons of Buffy, and was in 143 out of the 144 total episodes of the supernatural teen drama. Despite being an OG member of the Scooby Gang, the character hasn't exactly aged well as the years went by. Plenty of fans find his behavior to be misogynistic, specifically the way he refers to female characters like Cordelia, Anya, and (of course) Buffy herself. While some fans still love him, there are others who roll their eyes every time they re-watch the cult classic series.

Another character who I can get behind is none other than Owen Hunt from Grey's Anatomy. I'm personally pleased that Kevin McKidd has departed the medical drama, mostly because I can't stand the trauma surgeon. The comment itself reads:

i love greys anatomy but owen hunt is insufferable

Spoiler alert: the word "insufferable" is a common one in this Reddit thread. I regularly re-watch Grey's Anatomy, and every time I get mad about Owen all over again. Seriously, his relationship with Cristina Yang was a mess, largely thanks to his toxic masculinity. I mean, who can forget his reaction to Cristina's abortion back in Season 7? Then there's the way he strung Teddy along for years, as well as his being responsible for the plane crash that killed Sloan and Lexie.

While most of the characters in this thread have been supporting players, there are a few protagonists mentioned as well. Case in point: the following response about Orange is the New Black.

Piper in Orange is the new black. The show is great and I do recommend it to people, but I warn them beforehand that Piper is insufferable.

I told you "insufferable" was the word of the day. I recently re-watched Orange is the New Black, and I've got to say that I didn't hate Piper as much the second time around. That being said, she was one of my least favorite characters when the show was originally airing for those with a Netflix subscription. Mostly this was because of how much I adored supporting players like Taystee, as well as how she approached her time in prison from a place of privilege.

Some other characters named in this thread include Tara in Sons of Anarchy, Debbie in Shameless, Jenny from The L Word, and Tom Scavo from Desperate Housewives. I'm so behind the latter choice, because I've been rewatching the drama and I can't stand the way he treats Lynette.

What is your least favorite character from popular TV shows? Sound off in the comments section below. Smart money says that new titles arriving on the 2026 TV schedule are on that level. I'm looking at you, Ser Criston Cole from House of the Dragon.

#3685. 10 Shows Like 'The Diplomat' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Following its recently concluded fourth season, Netflix's political thriller The Diplomat has been renewed for a fifth season, and even better, it's the rare streaming show that seems to keep to a fairly regular schedule, meaning there's likely to be more of the Keri Russell-led espionage drama coming by late next year. If you're looking for something with the same political thriller vibes to watch in the meantime, here are 10 other series to stream now.

Diplomat creator Debora Cahn got her start on The West Wing, but honed her political-espionage craft on this show, for which she served as writer and, later, executive producer. The series begins with CIA case officer Carrie Mathison (Claire Danes) coming to suspect that decorated Marine Corps scout sniper Nicholas Brody (Damian Lewis), recently rescued from an al-Qaeda compound, has been turned and is planning a terrorist attack on the United States. As she has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, her superiors don't give Mathison's suspicions much credence, kicking off a cat-and-mouse/is-he-or-isn't he? game between the two. As the show progresses, Carrie moves up the ranks until she's working directly for the president. Both leads won Emmys for their performances, and the series took the Outstanding Drama prize in its first year. Stream Homeland on Hulu and Netflix.

Focusing largely on the seedier side of international espionage, Slow Horses, based on the novels by Mick Herron, shares with The Diplomat a dry sense of humor about the consequences of institutional and human failures. With nods to the great spy dramas of John le Carré, Slow Horses updates the setting without losing either the thrills or the style of a time-honored genre. The “Slow Horses” of the title are a group of has-been MI5 agents—they’ve all made messes of significant jobs, but are still seen as having some use, if only in dull administrative tasks. Naturally, the members of the group (led by Gary Oldman's endlessly flatulent Jackson Lamb) find themselves in deeper waters than anyone thought them capable of navigating. Kristin Scott Thomas is the spymaster, navigating political pressures, misogyny, and her own unrepentant ambition in trying to do her job. Stream Slow Horses on Apple TV.

An action drama that plays a bit like a spy thriller, The Night Agent stars Gabriel Basso as Peter Sutherland, an FBI agent who works overnights in the basement of the White House watching a phone that never, ever rings (dream job, honestly), until the night it does. Peter gets a call from Rose Larkin, a cybersecurity expert whose aunt and uncle were just killed; unbeknownst to her, they were also government operatives, and rescuing Rose sees Peter delving deep inside a web of conspiracy and corruption that plays out over three seasons, with a fourth and final on the way. While a bit more action-heavy than The Diplomat, it still plays in that realm of government secrets and conspiracies. Stream The Night Agent on Netflix.

There was a moment, around the turn of the millennium, when The West Wing seemed like a heightened but not entirely implausible picture of politics in action; its ripped-from-the-headlines style gave it an edge that allowed us to imagine smart, thoughtful people getting jobs in government, trying to do the more-or-less right thing despite systemic and personal flaws (it's also where The Diplomat's creator Debora Cahn started her TV writing career). The show's world can be a little frustrating when contrasted against our more explicitly appalling actual one, but it's a thoroughly pleasing fantasy nonetheless, with President Matin Sheen leading a White House staff through various diplomatic, military, and political crises. Stream The West Wing on Netflix and HBO Max.

Sidse Babett Knudsen stars as Birgitte Nyborg in this popular import. She's a minor Danish politician who watches other politicians fall to scandal and incompetence as she rapidly and unexpectedly ascends to the job of prime minister. The espionage and action are entirely incidental (but not nonexistent) here, as the show deals instead with the moral and political compromises that are seemingly intrinsic to statecraft. There's been talk of an American remake for years now, but you should just watch the original. Stream Borgen on Netflix.

Shonda Rhimes was already a powerhouse producer and screenwriter with several successful seasons of Grey's Anatomy under her belt when Scandal debuted, but its blend of political thrills and sexy, soapy drama truly solidified her brand—and her spot atop the modern TV landscape. Kerry Washington stars as Olivia Pope, head of the D.C.-based crisis management firm Olivia Pope & Associates (OPA), who is the person to call when you've got a PR disaster to fix. If you want to get a sense of the stakes involved, consider that Tony Goldwyn costars as Fitzgerald Grant III, who is both the president of the United States. and also Olivia's lover. Stream Scandal on Hulu and Netflix.

Téa Leoni plays Elizabeth McCord, a former CIA analyst who gave up that hectic life to become a political science professor. That's all going great until the Secretary of State dies under mysterious circumstances and she's called up by her old CIA boss, who's now the president, to take over the job. With her outsider's perspective and resistance to political considerations, she's surprisingly good at the gig, navigating foreign and domestic crises while also trying to figure out who the hell killed her predecessor, and whether they're coming for her, too. Stream Madam Secretary on The Roku Channel.

You could absolutely watch the original American take on this show, which stars Kiefer Sutherland—they have essentially the same premise—but this South Korean remake earns a few extra points by only running for a compact 16 episodes, making it far leaner and meaner. Education Minister Park Mu-jin (Ji Jin-hee) is fired from his job one day before an attack occurs amid an announcement of peace talks with the North, wiping out the entire presidential line of succession. His dismissal having not yet been finalized, the largely unambitious Minister Park is forced into the job, even as questions linger over the attack that put him in the role. Stream Designated Survivor: 60 Days on Netflix.

It's a different time and setting, but all the Keri Russell spy action you could want as a Diplomat fan. Set during the Cold War 1980s and created by former CIA officer Joe Weisberg, The Americans follows Soviet KGB intelligence agents Elizabeth (Russell) and Philip Jennings (the ever-reliable Matthew Rhys), living undercover lives posing as an American couple in the DC metro area—and raising their American-born children. The critically acclaimed show makes much of its period setting and a central conflict that places two spies in the heart of suburban America, even as they're tasked with undermining the Reagan-era government under which their children are growing up. Stream The Americans on Hulu.

A power struggle for leadership of an entire country is at the heart of this juicy political thriller. Prime Minister Park Dong-ho comes to believe that the president has been corrupted by powerful, wealthy individuals and companies (something that could only happen in South Korea, obviously). Deputy Prime Minister Jeong Su-jin sees the problem, too, but she's not so sure about his solution: He wants to have the president assassinated. But how much better is he than the man he would be replacing? And how pure are her motives in potentially putting herself in line for the top job? Stream The Whirlwind on Netflix.

The release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is basically a week away at this point. And as we get closer, Rockstar continues to release more marketing for the massive open-world sequel. Its latest move appears to be a gameplay clip showing off Vice City that tricked some people into thinking it was real footage.

On November 11, Florida-based Instagram account OnlyInDade posted a video showing off cool cars parked on a street in Miami. It’s the kind of content shot by people living in and around Miami that the account regularly posts. However, this wasn’t actually a real video recorded by someone in Miami. Instead, it is in-game footage from GTA 6.

With a Democratic midterm win, a mini AI crash in China, and Jensen Huang admitted to an affair this Sunday, Nvidia was already in a tight spot. Now, a second affair allegation has come out about Nvidia's CEO, and the AI company's share price has taken a hit as a result.

This reported second affair is said to be with another Nvidia exec, Kimberly Powell, and now the GPU company turned AI company is investigating whether or not it should oust the long-time CEO.

Naturally, that instability is worrisome to some investors, who appear to be signalling distrust towards the company in light of these scandals.

To put the stock dip into perspective, at close on Friday, Nvidia stock was worth $188.70 a share, a dip from a high of $239.24 on October 6. This morning, after-hours trading puts it at $161.88, as of the time of writing. We haven't seen a share price as low as this for Nvidia since well over a year ago, at the end of June 2025.

With this after-hours trading figure in mind, Nvidia's market cap (share price multiplied by outstanding shares) works out to around $3.93 trillion, which is just under half a trillion less than its market cap before the affair with Alice Huang came out (between $4.3 and $ 4.5 trillion).

Accounting for a share price of $173.73 at close yesterday, that would make a $300 billion dip overnight (from $4.2 to 3.9 trillion). Naturally, one can't assume that downward trajectory will continue to decline, but if Huang is in fact let go, Nvidia shares could see a further drop.

This doesn't mean Nvidia will be closing its doors tomorrow. In fact, it's still a hugely valuable company that remains a market leader in the AI hardware arms race. If you want a top-of-the-line AI chip, you're going to Nvidia before anyone else. And AI has proven to be excessively valuable over the last few years, turning Nvidia into the most valuable company in the world at one point (though Apple has since surpassed it).

Still, as the Nvidia board ruminates on whether or not to get rid of arguably its figurehead at this point, it's unclear where the company goes next and what it will do to regain that value. My bet is more and more AI and sadly not more affordable gaming GPUs. Sorry, people.

#3682. The JBL Vibe Beam Earbuds Are on Sale for $30 Right Now

If you want reliable earbuds that cost less than tonight's dinner, JBL is a reliable brand to fall back on, with plenty of budget-friendly models that lack the bells and whistles of pricier options while still delivering on sound and battery life. One of the most popular picks is the wireless JBL Vibe Beam earbuds, which are down 40% at $29.99 (originally $49.95).

These earbuds aren’t reinventing the wheel, but they do check important boxes. They last up to eight hours without the charging case, and up to 32 hours with the case. Ten minutes of charging will get you a couple of hours of playback, and they have an IP54 rating, making them dust- and splash-resistant. The built-in mics work well in reasonably quiet rooms, but may struggle to separate your voice from loud background noise. Another perk is Find My Buds, which helps locate misplaced earbuds via a sound that’s played.

With 8 mm dynamic drivers, they deliver punchy bass that translates well to adrenaline-pumping workout music, and adequate vocal clarity for music and podcasts. Though the default tuning is relatively balanced, you can tweak it on the app’s equalizer to adjust it to your liking. They lack ANC and Bluetooth multipoint pairing, which isn’t surprising given the price point, but still pack in a solid amount of features and quality into $30, making the wireless JBL Vibe Beam earbuds a good value for everyday bargain earbuds that get the job done.

During the merge episode of Survivor 51, the show included a shot of Brady Booker peeing on a tree. It was only a glimpse of his back for a few seconds, but it still attracted some attention from the fanbase because you almost never see it. Castaways talk about using the bathroom a lot, but they’re very rarely shown actually going. It turns out that’s because most of the going happens in one of the two places the crew isn’t allowed to film at.

Fan favorite multi-time player Kelley Wentworth, who produces some of the best Survivor content out there, dropped a video this week explaining how filming works and where the camerapeople aren’t allowed to go. Apparently, at the beginning of each season, castaways are told the crew will never film you in the so-called Coconut Grove, and they’ll never film you at the med box. Let’s talk about those two places separately.

Brady, however, didn’t use Coconut Grove during the most recent episode. He just let it rip on a random tree, which is why it was fair game for production to film him. Here’s how Wentworth put it…

Why were they filming him? Because he wasn’t peeing in Coconut Grove. He was just off pulling his thing out going to the bathroom on a tree right around camp… If you don’t go in the designated spot in CG, then yes, they absolutely can film you and they can absolutely put it in the episode.

To me, it’s pretty clear why Survivor decided to include the shot. They were building a narrative case in the edit that Brady was a big personality around camp that wasn’t always the most thoughtful, and that’s why, in addition to the peeing, we also got shots of his extreme eating and aggressive communicating, though in his defense, he did clarify that he thought he was alone.

In seasons past when we’ve seen contestants using the bathroom, it’s typically been related to building a narrative in the edit too, like when we saw Kathy pee on John Caroll’s hand after he was bit by a sea urchin, which helped her connect and find her place in the tribe or when we saw Christian accidentally poop his pants mid-conversation, which was a comedic and humbling moment. There's been clear purpose behind what we were shown, and I think there was in the Brady example too.

The other place Wentworth referenced that Survivor doesn’t ever film players at is the med box. Casuals may not know this, but the producers actually provide the players with some supplies that they’re allowed to use during the game. These might include things like contact solution, bug spray and medications the show’s doctors approved a particular contestant to take on the island. The women are also allowed to bring tampons, which one player famously used to smuggle in contraband. The show doesn’t want to break the immersive experience; so, that is also strictly a no filming zone.

Filming locations aside, Survivor 51 is, at least so far, one of the best seasons we’ve gotten of the show in a long time. The cast is filled with compelling personalities like Brady, and producers have shifted to a more unpredictable format that brings in elements from early seasons of the show (like gross food challenges). That combination has been a delight to watch, and if you haven’t given it a chance yet, I highly recommend you jump in. The water is warm this season, especially if someone is peeing right next to you.

Hideo KojimaKojima ProductionsOD: KnockPhysint

When Hideo Kojima rather suddenly left Konami in 2016 and, soon after, opened his own studio, the move sent shockwaves throughout the industry. Today, Kojima Productions has established itself as a AAA development studio within Japan known most of all for 3D-scanning celebrities and developing the Death Stranding franchise, which will soon move beyond gaming as it’s adapted into anime and a live-action film. Looking forward, the studio also plans to expand its range with Physint and OD: Knock in partnership with Xbox.

Itâs one of the more fascinating stories from the last decade of the Japanese games industry, not just for how Kojima Productions came to be but for how it’s sustained itself as a studio. Kojima has leaned on his name recognition to turn the studio into a brand unto itself, and the director keeps himself and the studio in the spotlight through an array of film work, social media posts, radio shows, cameos in TV dramas, and more.

In the upmarket area of Azabudai in central Tokyo, with the historic Tokyo Tower landmark in view, an exhibition looking back on the past decade of the studio has opened for a limited time. Not just chronicling the public history of the studio, the event also featured new information and unseen concept art for Death Stranding, alongside details about the company’s in-development Xbox titles. After visiting the exhibition during its opening days earlier this week, here are ten things we learned about the studio and its array of upcoming titles.

When this exhibition was first announced, Kojima Productions promised not just a look back at the past 10 years of the studio, but a look forward at its in-development work on Physint and OD: Knock as well. That said, actual new information about Physint was light, perhaps as a result of the gameâs turbulent summer which saw publishing shift from Sony to Xbox. All we could gather about work on that game came from some key concepts visible on a display copy of the gameâs script.

Though behind glass, the hefty document made a few significant bits of information aboutÂ Physint visible, providing our first hint about the setting of this new game. Notably, this game will take place within what the script callsÂ  âThe Next Cold War.â This war is defined by three philosophies: HUMINT (“human intelligence”), SIGINT (“signals intelligence,” whatever that may entail, perhaps involving communication in some way), and OSINT (“open-source intelligence”). From this, it seems likely that the term PHYSINT refers to something along the lines of physical intelligence, but thatâs still unconfirmed.

On the scriptâs cover, it appears that there’s a word that comes after Physint and has been redacted, suggesting we don’t yet know the game’s full, final title. We also saw some models of things that appear in-game, including a few mechs that look suspiciously like Metal Gear. Considering Kojima referred to the title as being in the same vein as his earlier stealth series, that’s not entirely unsurprising.

Kojima Productions has become more than a studio: itâs a brand. The merchandise featuring the studioâs logo and spacesuit-wearing Lumens character is proof of this. It appears that having a striking logo was a consideration from early on, as we got a rare look into the design process for the logo and mascot at the show. Notably, while the current logo features a skull inside a spacesuit and emphasizes the head of the character, many of the early designs featured the full character waving a flag. Another shows a knighted character that looks somewhat like Raiden from the Metal Gear series.

While most of the exhibit allowed visitors to freely snap photos of all the concept art and design documents on display, photography was restricted on a short video containing footage of the original prototype for Death Stranding. Luckily, at least part of this video has been shared by Famitsu.

Even in this early state, the game looks rather close to the final release. It seems the concept of running around a sparse, mountainous setting was decided, and we can see rough gameplay of a generic character model picking up cargo and moving around the environment. Another piece of footage shown, taken from further along in development, gives an early glimpse of how BTs were implemented in the game. Theyâre shown acting for more aggressively than they do in the final game, suggesting the emphasis on combat was somewhat toned down before release.

While some concept art for the original Death Stranding has been released to the public via art books, a lot of never-before-seen artwork and footage for the game was shown at the event, making up a sizable portion of the exhibit. This included early attempts at a logo, original sketches by designer Yoji Shinkawa, and more.

Particularly notable, however, were the screens on various walls showing behind-the-scenes footage of motion capture and how the designs for each character changed during development. Early cutscenes were printed on planning documents with Kojimaâs handwritten notes (in amusingly shiny gel pen). And, of course, we got a brief look at the baby doll that was used during these sessions, and the original 3D-printed prototype for the Pods that hold the BBs in the game.

Summaries of documents sent to Sony during the planning stage of Death Stranding to secure support from the company were also on display. These documents explain the concept of “Strand” gameplay as a genre in which multiple players indirectly interact in the same space. The documents also convey that the concept of the game is to âunite us allâ through your actions as you traverse the United States. Early concept art for all of the major characters, including a vastly different version of Fragile, are also on display.

The game’s complex development pipeline was also documented in images that were on display, conveying just how many differing, simultaneous tasks a team must undertake to take a game from concept to finished product within AAA game development.

While some call the first Death Stranding prophetic for how its concepts of connection and delivery were later realized in real life when the world shut down during the Covid-19 pandemic, it turns out Death Stranding 2âs story was radically reworked to consider the altered state of the world as everything shut down to prevent the spread of the virus.

Based on documents shown at the event, the first concept for Death Stranding 2 was produced in 2017, toward the end of development on the first game. Most notable from these documents is a vastly different ending to the game compared to the one we actually gotâa far more optimistic and positive one. The fate of all the characters is revealed, with Fragile alive and leading a delivery team, and Rainy and Tomorrow raising a baby together.

The document also details subterranean gameplay that would allow for greater variety in traversal, though the overall concept of connecting the world was present from this early state. It also appears that even at this time, Elle Fanning had already been considered for Tomorrow, as her name is brought up in the document.

We will be exhibiting âMADO,â a telepresence system that enables seamless two-way communication between remote locations. We used it during the COVID-19 pandemic for performance capture sessions connecting Los Angeles and Tokyo. Throughout the exhibition, âMADOâ will continuouslyâ¦ https://t.co/Y7Jc3HzYJG pic.twitter.com/oxwhnpvQGS

— HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) October 18, 2026

To aid in development, and especially with scanning actors and conducting motion capture when borders were closed during the pandemic, Kojima Productions developed its own communication system to aid in networking with actors and remote workers, known as Mado (Japanese for âwindowâ). Developed by MUSVI Corporation, Mado was used to connect people in a more immersive manner than a mere video call could allow for. Kojima Productions used it to connect with motion capture studios in Los Angeles for more effective direction of actors during these sessions, even when separated across different countries and time zones.

For the exhibition, the technology was on display with a direct feed to the Kojima Productions office in real time, providing a so-called window into the studio. During our visit, this showed the area in the studio where 3D scans of actors are done, but it seems that this will be changed up throughout the event.
